intro: If you're driving through Chai Nat or visiting the Bird Park and want a stay that's in town, on the main road, affordable, with breakfast and easy parking — Chainatgrand Hotel (Chainat Grand) is a tidy fit for a mid-range budget. It's a 3-star, 63-room in-town hotel on Phahonyothin Road, Ban Kluai Subdistrict, Mueang Chai Nat District. The draw is clean air-conditioned rooms, an elevator, an on-site restaurant, free parking, free Wi-Fi and a 24-hour front desk. It's just a few minutes' drive from the Chainat Walking Street and the Bird Park. Rooms start at around ฿800/night — the trade-off being a plain in-town hotel with no pool, but if you just need a good-value bed in town, it delivers.

body.html: Chainatgrand Hotel — known locally as Chainat Grand — is a 3-star, 63-room in-town hotel on Phahonyothin Road, Ban Kluai Subdistrict, Mueang Chai Nat District. It's a multi-storey building with an elevator. The selling point isn't flashy design or a long list of facilities, but a main-road in-town location, clean rooms, low prices and an on-site restaurant — ideal for travellers who care more about a good-value bed than atmosphere.

What reviews praise most often is the handy location, the value for money, and the generous parking. Many describe the rooms as clean, with easy access right on Phahonyothin Road, close to convenience stores and city sights. There's an on-site restaurant, Tha Phra Chanthon, serving Thai and Chinese dishes plus local freshwater-fish specialities. It's the kind of place that works well as an overnight stop on the road, or as a base for exploring central Chai Nat.
"Great location right on the main road, easy in and out, clean rooms and plenty of parking. Good value for a quick overnight stop on the road."

Rooms come in several types, from Standard and Superior doubles up to Deluxe and Triple rooms with three single beds for groups or families. Every room is air-conditioned with a flat-screen TV, fridge, hot water and a private bathroom. The look is plain, bright and clean — not luxurious, but everything works. Most reviews call the rooms clean and good value for the price tier.

On facilities, it covers the in-town hotel basics. There's an elevator, free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, an on-site restaurant and a function room for up to 120 guests. The limit to note is that there's no pool, and breakfast means choosing a room that includes it or paying extra. But with the in-town setting, eating out nearby is easy, with plenty of shops and markets around.

On scores, Chainatgrand sits in the good range for the in-town group — Trip.com gives it around 8.7, though from a still-small review base, while TripAdvisor lands mid-range with one notably critical review about service. The recurring praise is for the in-town location, clean rooms, ample parking and value. The criticisms that come up are an older building, some rooms smaller than expected, dust in corners, and service that's sometimes inflexible. These are typical trade-offs of an affordable in-town hotel.

To be honest, Chainatgrand Hotel isn't for travellers chasing atmosphere or photogenic design. Its appeal is being a clean in-town hotel with an elevator, an on-site restaurant, free parking and a main-road location, from around ฿800. A standard room in normal periods runs about ฿800–1,000, while Deluxe and Triple rooms go up to around ฿1,220, rising over long weekends and festivals. If your trip is a drive through Chai Nat, a Bird Park visit, or you want a good-value base in town, this works. If you want a resort with a pool or a riverside feel, look at higher-priced stays instead.

A tip from reading the reviews: this suits drivers and road-trip stopovers best, thanks to the wide parking and main-road setting. Travelling as a group or family? The Triple room with three single beds is better value than booking two standard rooms. Check whether your room includes breakfast when you book — if it does, it's better value and handier than heading out. And compare prices across platforms before booking, since in-town hotels like this swing clearly with season and each site's deals.

faq.q: Where is Chainatgrand Hotel — is it in town?
faq.a: It's at 309/30 Phahonyothin Road, Ban Kluai, Mueang Chai Nat District — an in-town hotel on the main road, about 1.6 km from the Chainat Walking Street and Lieng Hin Dam, and roughly 3 km from the Chainat Bird Park. The location is easy to reach with ample parking, handy for self-drivers.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: From around ฿800/night in normal periods. There are Standard and Superior doubles, plus Deluxe and Triple rooms (three single beds) at around ฿1,220 for more space or for groups. Every room is air-conditioned with a TV, fridge and hot water. Prices rise over long weekends and festivals, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is there an elevator, parking and Wi-Fi — any breakfast or pool?
faq.a: There's an elevator, free ample parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk and an on-site restaurant. Breakfast means choosing a room that includes it or paying extra. There is no pool. The upside is the in-town setting, with plenty of places to eat nearby.

faq.q: What are the rooms and cleanliness like?
faq.a: Most rooms are clean, well-equipped and good value for the in-town tier. Some reviews mention an older building, rooms smaller than expected and dust in corners. Ask to see the room at check-in or request a change if you're not happy.

faq.q: What's the review score and who is it best for?
faq.a: The real score sits in the good range for the in-town group — around 8.7 on Trip.com, though from a still-small review base. It's a strong fit for self-drive travellers, road-trip stopovers and anyone wanting a clean, good-value base in central Chai Nat. If you want a pool or a resort feel, look elsewhere.
